chapter_title: Checking and Calibrating AI Agent Output
learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of eight quotations offered by an agent is an exact quote, an altered quote, or not in the text, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** quote-verifier
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of eight quotations offered by an agent is an exact quote, an altered quote, or not in the text, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Hallucination, Evidence for a Score (defined in Chapter 3), Agent Evaluation Report (defined in Chapter 12) (all defined in this chapter above this block or in earlier chapters). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each quotation the learner commits one of three verdicts. A verdict is correct when it matches the Correct verdict column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Rereading the excerpt is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A quotation that sounds right is exact. (2) A small change to a quotation does not matter. (3) A quotation that is plausible must be somewhere in the text. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging a quotation against its source is an Evaluate-level action that every review of an agent's evidence needs. Altered quotations, which differ in one detail, teach the learner to compare word for word, and invented ones teach the learner to search the whole text. **Content:** The excerpt, shown at all times (made up): "Watershed Basics by Maria Lopez. Licensed under CC BY 4.0. A watershed is an area of land where all the water drains to the same place. Section 2: The Clearwater River drains about 6,000 square miles and flows into Lake Marlow. Figure 1: A map of the Clearwater watershed. Alt text: A map showing the river and its tributaries. Quiz: Question 1 asks the learner to choose the definition of a watershed." The three verdicts: Exact quote, Altered quote, Not in the text. The eight quotations: | # | Quotation offered by the agent | Correct verdict | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | "Licensed under CC BY 4.0" | Exact quote | The words appear exactly. | | 2 | "A watershed is an area of land where all the water drains to the same place." | Exact quote | The sentence appears exactly. | | 3 | "The Clearwater River drains about 6,000 square miles and flows into the sea." | Altered quote | The excerpt says it flows into Lake Marlow, so "the sea" is a change. | | 4 | "Captions are available in English and Spanish." | Not in the text | Nothing in the excerpt mentions captions. | | 5 | "Figure 1: A map of the Clearwater watershed." | Exact quote | The caption appears exactly. | | 6 | "Alt text: A detailed map of the river, its tributaries, and nearby towns." | Altered quote | The excerpt says "A map showing the river and its tributaries", so details were added. | | 7 | "Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0" | Altered quote | The excerpt says CC BY, so the license was changed. | | 8 | "An answer key is included for all quiz questions." | Not in the text | Nothing in the excerpt mentions an answer key. | **Provenance:** The excerpt and quotations are made up for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The verdicts follow the chapter section "Hallucination". **Rules:** Each quotation has exactly one correct verdict. Three are Exact quote, three are Altered quote, and two are Not in the text. A quotation is exact only when it matches the excerpt word for word. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the excerpt and one quotation. 2. The learner chooses a verdict, and the choice is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text, and highlights the matching or conflicting part of the excerpt. 4. After quotation 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 quotations in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [verdict]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [verdict]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can check an agent's quotations." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed quotation. **Starting State:** The excerpt and quotation 1 or the first quotation in the shuffled order. The question shown is "Does this quotation appear in the text?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists four forms of hallucination: an invented feature, quotation, measurement, and source. The chapter's worked example includes an altered alt text for a map.
